key_claims.claim: Continuous doula support likely reduces preterm birth and cesarean delivery rates and improves patient-reported birth experience, based on pooled data from 12 RCTs and 18 non-randomized studies with moderate GRADE certainty.
Safety data on GLP-1 receptor agonist exposure around conception remain sparse, with no clear teratogenic signal but significant counseling gaps for clinicians managing these patients.
A reduced in-person antenatal visit schedule supplemented by telemedicine appears non-inferior to standard care for maternal and neonatal outcomes in low-risk pregnancies.
Selective reduction in monochorionic pregnancies with selective fetal growth restriction yields quantifiable co-twin demise and delivery gestational age rates that differ by technique.
Individual severe-feature criteria in preeclampsia confer differential perinatal risk, allowing more granular prognostic stratification than the composite diagnosis alone.
